adoptedBy: Profile (with its language and logout sheets)
scope.note: Other screens, the floating bottom navigation, PortalShell, and its offline banner still render the previous violet system (earlier AppColors tokens and AppSurfaces) and migrate one screen at a time.

mist-25.source: derived: slate-100 a quarter of the way to white

onError.note: Content on an error fill, such as the destructive logout confirm.

insetShade.note: Shade along the top inner edge of a shape cut into a surface (the badge's lanyard slot); always blended over the ground, never a fill on its own.

systemBars.iconBrightness: dark icons in Light, light icons in Dark

display.purpose: Screen headline, such as the sign-in welcome and the Profile page title (Material headlineMedium).

title.purpose: A person's name or a sheet title: the badge name, the badge initials, the language and logout sheet titles (Material titleLarge).

brand.purpose: Product name in the ticket stub (Material titleMedium).

body-large.purpose: A headline's supporting line and a sheet's message.

body-medium.purpose: Notices and help lines; the error notice raises it to 600. Badge labels (muted) and status values (muted, 500).

row-title.purpose: Body Large tightened for a settings row or sheet option; a selected language option raises it to 700.

value.purpose: Body Medium raised for data with tabular figures: badge values in the title role, row values in the body role.

label.purpose: Label above a field (Material labelLarge) and Profile's section labels (muted, sentence case); the pending count raises it to 700 with tabular figures.

data.purpose: Small tabular data fields such as the stub's issue date.

typographyMeta.fontNote: Platform system fonts: Roboto on Android, SF Pro on iOS, the platform's native Arabic face. No bundled faces in this phase. Sizes are dp.

shadows.name: raised-light
shadows.purpose: The ticket or ID badge in Light: soft ambient drop plus a faint contact edge. Flutter blurRadius values carried as CSS blur.

shadows.name: raised-dark
shadows.purpose: The ticket or ID badge in Dark.

motion.name: ticket-rise
motion.purpose: Cold-start entrance of the ticket; no fade. Skipped when a route transition brings the page in or reduced motion is on.

motion.name: fade-through-in
motion.value: 320ms; ground cover 0-35% ease-out; content fade 35-100% cubic-bezier(0.33, 1, 0.68, 1) with scale 0.96 to 1
motion.purpose: Route transition between screens in this world (Login and Home). Skipped when system animations are off.

motion.name: action-swap
motion.purpose: Primary action label and arrow swap for the loading spinner.

motion.name: value-swap
motion.value: 180ms cross-fade, ease-out-cubic cubic-bezier(0.215, 0.61, 0.355, 1), anchored to the end edge
motion.purpose: A changed badge value, row value, or pending count replaces the old one in place without moving its row. Instant under reduced motion.

shapes.perforation: 1px dashed, 6px dash, 5px gap, inset 8px from each notch, hairline color
shapes.badgeRadius: 20px, 1px hairline border, no notches or perforation
shapes.lanyardSlot: 40x8px, 4px radius, centred 12px below the badge top; vertical gradient from insetShade over ground (0) to ground (45%)
shapes.rowDivider: 1px hairline between rows, inset 20px from each side

narrative.overview:
Every surface in this world reads like a fuel or weighbridge ticket handed to a driver: a stub that says who issued it and when, a perforated tear line, and a working body below. The paper is calm and the ink is official. The palette is the binding slate-navy six, built into two schemes that are designed separately rather than inverted: Light is a mist ground with a white ticket and ink action; Dark is an ink ground with a lifted navy ticket and a mist action. Depth comes from one soft shadow on the one raised surface and from fields that sit tonally below the ticket.

The same paper and ink also issue the driver's company ID. Profile is one laminated badge, white on mist in Light and lifted navy on ink in Dark, with a punched lanyard slot at its top and a hairline-ruled grid of labels and values. Everything the driver can change sits loose on the ground below it in hairline-divided rows, never boxed in cards.

Density is low and deliberate. A surface shows the few things the driver needs, at a size that survives a cab in daylight, a night shift, a large system font, and Arabic as much as English. Decoration is limited to each issued document's own anatomy: the ticket's notches, perforation, and route mark; the badge's lanyard slot and label-value grid. Motion is short, purposeful, and always skipped when the system asks for reduced motion.

Scope: this world is adopted by Login and Profile, including Profile's language and logout sheets. Every other screen, the floating bottom navigation, `PortalShell`, and its offline banner still render the previous violet system (the earlier tokens in `AppColors` and the `AppSurfaces` roles) and migrate one screen at a time. This document governs only surfaces built on `AppPalette`.
keyCharacteristics: Official slate-navy only; no saturated hue anywhere except a muted error red.
Two built schemes with their own roles, read through `AppPalette`.
One raised surface per screen, with one soft shadow: the ticket on Login, the ID badge on Profile.
Hairline borders; controls share one 12dp corner.
The perforated tear line with side notches is the ticket's signature; the lanyard slot and label-value grid are the badge's.
Lists sit on the ground, divided by 1dp hairlines.
Platform system fonts, no negative tracking, tabular figures for data.

rules.name: The Official Six Rule
rules.body: Every neutral is one of the six official values or a stated mix of them (mist is slate-100 toward white; slate-450 and slate-350 sit between slate-600 and slate-300). New colors are derived the same way, never picked freely.

rules.name: The Built Twice Rule
rules.body: Light and Dark are two designed role sets, not an inversion: the Dark field sinks to the ground color, and the Dark action turns pale. Screens read roles from `AppPalette`, never raw tokens.

rules.name: The Joined Letters Rule
rules.body: Letter spacing stays at normal on every role so Arabic letters stay joined. Hierarchy comes from size and weight.

rules.name: The Tabular Data Rule
rules.body: Dates, amounts, and any figure that may line up with another use tabular figures.

rules.name: The One Raised Surface Rule
rules.body: A screen has one raised surface: the ticket on Login, the ID badge on Profile. Fields, notices, buttons, and rows do not cast shadows.

rules.name: The Perforation Rule
rules.body: The tear line separates a ticket's identifying stub from its working body. It appears once per ticket and is never used as a generic divider. It stays the ticket's: the badge's grid and Profile's rows are divided by solid hairlines.

dos: **Do** read colors through `AppPalette` roles so each scheme gets its own built value.
**Do** keep one raised surface per screen, carrying `raisedShadow`.
**Do** put every control on the 12dp corner and every border on a 1dp hairline; only focus thickens to 1.6dp.
**Do** keep touch targets at least 48dp and merge a field's visible label into its semantics.
**Do** lay list rows on the ground at 56dp or more, divided by 1dp hairlines inset 20dp.
**Do** end-align values and swap a changed value in place (180ms ease-out-cubic cross-fade) without moving its row.
**Do** mirror directional icons (arrows, chevrons) in right-to-left.
**Do** put content on an error fill in `onError`, as content on an action fill uses `onAction`.
**Do** skip every entrance, transition, and value swap when the system asks for reduced motion.
donts: **Don't** introduce saturated colors; the error red stays muted and is the only hue outside the slate-navy ladder.
**Don't** use the previous violet tokens (`AppColors.primary` and its siblings, `AppSurfaces`) on a surface that has moved to this world.
**Don't** invert Light to make Dark; each scheme has its own role values.
**Don't** apply negative letter spacing on any role.
**Don't** add shadows to fields, notices, buttons, or rows, or stack a second raised card on the ticket or badge.
**Don't** box list rows in cards; they lie on the ground.
**Don't** use the perforation as a plain divider in lists or sections, or give the badge a stub, notches, or perforation.
**Don't** fade the ticket in on entrance; it rises once, already visible. The rise stays the ticket's.
